rendered:
The NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a narrow pH window of roughly 10[1] to 12[2]. The reason is that simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is difficult because their hydroxides have different solubility products (Ksp). Aluminum hydroxide starts precipitating at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate only beyond[3] . Keeping the pH inside this window is what makes the successful synthesis of NFA precursors in hydroxide form possible.

How the precursors become cathode powder: the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors.[4] These precursors are then mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures >600 °C[5]. After calcination the NFA cathode powder is obtained, which is then cast into electrodes by roll-to-roll slot-die coating for cobalt-free pouch cell assembly.
